problem: The point $H$ has spherical polar coordinates $(\sqrt{3},\frac{4\pi }{3},\frac{5\pi }{6}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $H.$

feedback.problem: The point $D$ has spherical coordinates $(\sqrt{2},\pi ,\frac{\pi }{4}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $D.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Calculating $x$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot (-1)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $y$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot 0\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $z$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $D$ are $(-1,0,1).$
